Gas supply to national grid restored as damaged LNG terminal resumes partial operation
item.description:
One boiler at the damaged floating LNG (liquefied natural gas) terminal in Moheshkhali, Cox's Bazar, has resumed operation. As a result, gas supply to the national grid has partially resumed, and pressure in Chattogram's gas pipelines has begun to improve. PetroBangla has confirmed the development.

Today, Thursday, unlike the previous several days, long queues of vehicles were no longer seen at CNG filling stations across the city. Many drivers were able to refill their vehicles within the usual time.

Speaking to Prothom Alo on Thursday afternoon, PetroBangla Director (Operations) Md Rafiqul Islam said one boiler at the damaged LNG terminal was restarted at around 3:00 am last night after repairs were completed.

LPG prices rise amid gas supply shortage

The terminal is now supplying 115 million cubic feet of gas per day to the national grid. Another floating terminal in Moheshkhali is supplying an additional 550 million cubic feet daily. As a result, the overall situation has begun to improve, he added.

Mohammad Rafique Khan, deputy general manager of Karnaphuli Gas Distribution Company Limited (KGDCL), which is responsible for gas supply in Chattogram, told Prothom Alo, “Yesterday we received 183 million cubic feet of gas. Today we are receiving even more. Pressure in the pipelines has also increased. The situation has improved.”

Chattogram had been experiencing a severe gas shortage for the past several days. Technical problems at the Moheshkhali LNG terminal reduced gas supply to the national grid, causing widespread disruption to industries, CNG filling stations and households.

In many areas, gas stoves remained unusable for hours. Drivers had to wait in queues for five to eight hours at filling stations, with many spending the night in their vehicles.

However, visits on Thursday to Mir CNG Filling Station at City Gate, Paharika Filling Station in Akbar Shah and Fossil Filling Station in Sholoshahar showed significantly fewer customers than on previous days. There were no long queues, and drivers were able to refill their vehicles after comparatively shorter waits.

In Frames: Wheels at a standstill in search of gas

A fire broke out at the floating LNG terminal operated by Excelerate Energy in Moheshkhali on 21 July. Gas supply to the national grid declined afterwards, affecting Chattogram and several other parts of the country.

Chattogram's daily gas demand is around 350 million cubic feet. Over the past few days, however, supply had fallen to 190–200 million cubic feet, leaving the city with a shortfall of nearly half its daily requirement.

Officials concerned said the resumption of one boiler at the damaged terminal would significantly ease the shortage for now. Gas supply is expected to return to a more normal level once the terminal becomes fully operational.

item.title: EC: Presidential election on August 20
item.description:
The Election Commission (EC) on Thursday announced the schedule for the presidential election, with voting set to take place on August 20.
EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed announced the schedule at a press conference at Nirbachan Bhaban in the capital on Thursday.
According to the schedule, nomination papers will be submitted from 10am to 4pm on August 13.
Scrutiny of nomination papers will be held on August 16, while the last date for withdrawal of candidature is August 18.
Voting will take place from 2pm to 5pm on August 20 in the session chamber of the National Parliament.
Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin is the returning officer of the presidential election.
Earlier, the EC received the voter list for the presidential election from the Parliament Secretariat following its request. The voting will not be held in case of a single candidate.
On July 24 last, Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned as president and Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad took charge as the acting president.
The EC, led by Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin, held a meeting with acting Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal on July 28 in line with the Presidential Election Act, 1991, which obliges the Commission to consult with the Speaker before the announcement of the schedule for the presidential election.
According to Article 123(2) of the Constitution, an election to fill the vacant office of the President must be held within 90 days of the post becoming vacant due to resignation.

Prime Minister’s Finance and Planning Adviser Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir on Thursday said Bangladesh’s existing fragile economy must be transformed into a trillion-dollar one, converging the nation’s development trajectory and its five-year strategic plan with global frameworks.
He stressed the need for synchronization with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and the Paris Agreement.
Titumir called for private-capital mobilization and the need for global climate funds to match national ambition with speed and concessionality, as well as reflected on the philosophy of the premier as set out in BNP’s election manifesto.
The adviser made the suggestions while addressing the closing session of an Economic Relations Division (ERD)-sponsored event in the capital.
The ERD hosted the High-Level Policy Dialogue at a hotel in the capital on the theme “Building Bangladesh a Trillion-Dollar Climate-Resilient Economy: Accelerating Climate Finance Mobilization through Designing Strategic & Investment-Ready Climate Projects”.
Organized under the Bangladesh Climate Development Partnership (BCDP), the event marked the 33rd initiative of ERD’s International Climate Finance Cell (ICFC).
Asian Development Bank (ADB) extended technical support for the dialogue that brought together policy leaders, international financial institutions, private-sector executives, civil society organizations and academia, said an ERD press release.
The dialogue formed Round 2 of ICFC’s flagship capacity-building program, “From Vision to Approval: Unlocking GCF Finance through High-Impact Concept Notes.”
Building on Round 1 — a series of online introductory sessions — it prepares participants for Round 3, a residential Climate Leadership Incubation Lab in which they will author investment-ready Green Climate Fund (GCF) concept notes under expert mentorship.
ERD’s UN wing chief AKM Sohel delivered the opening note, outlining the objectives of the initiative, while the inaugural session was joined by ERD secretary Md Shahriar Kader Siddiky.
Siddiky noted that Bangladesh was losing a great deal due to climate change and must focus sharply on climate financing.
He called for a strong structure to crowd in private investment — candidly acknowledging that the country remains behind in its readiness to submit proposals to international climate funds.
Emphasizing partnership, innovation and shared prosperity, he affirmed that securing climate finance is a collective responsibility grounded in strong project ownership.
The session also featured remarks from ADB Country Director Qingfeng Zhang, who reaffirmed ADB’s continued commitment to partnering with Bangladesh on climate-resilient development and emphasized the importance of designing bankable, investment-ready projects to mobilise climate finance at scale.
The policy dialogue proceeded through two comprehensive thematic panel sessions, each anchored by a keynote presentation from AKM Sohel, Wing Chief of the UN Wing at ERD, who framed climate literacy as the vital bridge between scientific reality and financial feasibility, and outlined the strategic pathway to transform climate science into fundable theories of change.
